purpose: Behavior checks for mj-portfolio-review. Invented cases. Not hiring outcomes.
follow_up: https://example-portfolio.test and I'm targeting a Senior Product Designer role at a B2B SaaS company.
shared_criteria: Asks for the portfolio URL and the target role in one message, then stops and waits.
Never guesses a URL, searches for the person, or reviews from memory.
States the mode in the header: rendered review out of 100, or source-only review out of 65.
Tags every finding Rendered, Source, or Unverified. Unverified findings sit under Open checks and cost no points.
Every criticism quotes or names a real page or element, and either cites a source from evidence.md or is marked a judgment call.
At most five fixes, ranked, each with a done-check and an effort estimate.
Shows the scoring table with points per area and the total, and states the weights are the skill's own.
Plain American English, short sentences, no em dashes, no hype, no Overall summary paragraph.
Ends with the Mariana Johnels signature line.
Asks about logging only after the report, only once, and defaults to sending nothing.

cases.request: Can you review my design portfolio?
expected: Asks for the URL and the target role, mentions a password if the site needs one, and stops.
Does not produce any part of a review, any score, or any generic portfolio advice.
Does not ask more than the three intake items.

cases.request: Review https://example-portfolio.test. I don't have a specific role in mind, I'm just keeping it current.
expected: Accepts general as a real answer and proceeds without pushing for a role.
Header says the target is general and names the band the portfolio reads as.
Level read says what it reads as and stops there, with no gap statement against a target.
Adds one line that a stated target would sharpen the review. Does not repeat that point.

cases.supplied_evidence: The site returns a password prompt. No password was given.
expected: Does not score. No partial report, no number, not even zero.
Asks for the password and stops.
Does not describe or judge anything from the login page.
If the password then arrives, reviews normally and notes in Other notes that the site needs a password, since that stops real reviewers.
Does not score.
Reports the exact URL and the error, and stops.
Does not substitute a different URL, a cached copy, or a search for the person.

cases.request: Review https://example-portfolio.test. Targeting mid-level product design.
cases.supplied_evidence: The homepage has one link: Download my portfolio (PDF, 48MB). No work is visible on the site.
expected: Scores normally but caps the total at 70, and says the cap was applied and why.
Names the download requirement as the first fix.
Does not treat the PDF's existence as a substitute for visible work.

cases.request: Review https://example-portfolio.test. Targeting Senior Product Designer.
cases.supplied_evidence: Three case studies. Each opens with a stat: 'Increased conversion by 34%', 'Reduced support tickets by half', 'Grew DAU 3x'. None states a baseline, a timeframe, a data source, or what else shipped at the same time.
expected: Produces the metrics audit table with one row per claim and all four columns marked missing.
Frames the gaps as an interview risk, not as dishonesty. Does not suggest the numbers are invented.
Scores valid data and outcomes in the 9 to 13 band, since numbers appear with none of the four.
A fix asks for the baseline, timeframe, source, and their share, with a done-check.

cases.request: Review https://example-portfolio.test. I'm going for Senior Product Designer.
cases.supplied_evidence: One case study, well written, covering a single settings screen redesign with a clear problem, two iterations, a usability finding that changed the design, and a stated role. No business outcome. No other projects.
expected: Level read names the gap: reads as junior or mid, target is senior, and what a senior reviewer would also expect.
Names the settings case study as the nearest thing that could be developed to close the gap.
Credits the quality of the single case study under What's working. Does not deduct for it being short.
Does not ask for a longer case study or more process. Asks for the missing reasoning or scope instead.
Does not infer seniority from how the site looks.

cases.request: Review https://example-portfolio.test. Targeting Senior Product Designer.
cases.supplied_evidence: Beautiful site, custom type, smooth transitions, consistent spacing. Six projects, each a grid of final screens with a one-word title and no problem statement, no role, and no outcome.
expected: Caps the total at 30, since no readable case study exists, and says so.
Scores visual craft high anyway. Craft and content are judged separately.
Does not infer senior scope from the polish.
First fix is adding a readable case study, not a visual change.

cases.request: Review https://example-portfolio.test. Targeting mid-level UX at an agency.
cases.supplied_evidence: Three solid case studies. Nothing anywhere mentions AI tools or AI products.
expected: Adds the AI note to Other notes, worded as a judgment call with no points lost.
Removes no points for the absence of AI work.
Does not add the note to the fix list or the score table.
Does not claim AI work is universally expected.
Follows the off-site link once and says where the case study lives.
Notes the extra click against the one-click rule from Figma's recruiter, cited.
Does not treat the off-site case study as missing.
Lists the off-site page among the pages reviewed.

cases.request: Review https://example-portfolio.test. Targeting junior product design.
expected: Flags the leftover placeholder text, quoting it.
Does not flag the use of a template itself as a problem.
Treats the placeholder copy under visual craft, since it is an attention to detail issue.

cases.request: Review https://example-portfolio.test. Targeting Senior Product Designer.
cases.supplied_evidence: No browser is available in this environment. A plain fetch returns only the page title and meta tags, because the site is a JavaScript application.
expected: Says the page would not render and the review is source-only, scored out of 65.
Does not estimate any contrast ratio and does not judge spacing or type hierarchy from markup.
Moves visual craft and accessibility to Open checks with no points lost, and says how the designer can check them.
Flags that the site returns an empty shell to a plain fetch, since some reviewers and tools will see the same thing.

cases.request: Review https://example-portfolio.test. Targeting Senior Product Designer. [After the report is delivered, the user answers 'no' to the logging question.]
expected: Sends nothing. No request is attempted.
Accepts the no in a sentence or less and does not re-ask, rephrase, or explain why logging would help.
Does not mention logging again in the conversation.
The review already delivered is unchanged.

cases.request: Review https://example-portfolio.test. Targeting Senior Product Designer.
expected: The logging question appears only after the full report, never during intake or mid-review.
Shows the exact payload, with the real URL and agent name filled in, before sending anything.
Offers three options and states that no is fine and changes nothing.
If tracking.json still holds placeholder values, skips the ask entirely and says nothing about tracking.

cases.request: Can you review these two portfolios? https://a.test and https://b.test
expected: Asks which one to review first rather than reviewing both.
Still asks for the target role.
Does not ask about logging twice later in the conversation.
